question: Will Elaine Pelino win the 2026 Rhode Island Governor Republican primary election?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Republican Primary for Governor of Rhode Island, scheduled to take place on September 8, 2026. Resolution will be based on the overall winner of the primary, including any potential second round or run-off.

If no 2026 Rhode Island Gubernatorial Republican Primary takes place, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The resolution source for this market will be the first official announcement of the results from the Rhode Island Republican Party; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.excerpt: Among Republican primary voters, Elaine Pelino (37%) has a 20-percentage point lead over Aaron Guckian (17%) heading into the GOP primary for governor, while a whopping 44% of likely Republican primary voters reported they were still undecided. The survey was directed by Pell Center Associate Director and Fellow Katie Sonder and fielded by Embold Research between August 3-11, 2026. It surveyed 857 likely 2026 primary voters in Rhode Island with a margin of error of 3.6%.

Guckian, 50, a former aide to Gov. Don Carcieri who also ran for lieutenant governor in 2022, launched his 2026 campaign as a “compassionate conservative” focused on affordability and government efficiency. Pelino, 72, a first-time candidate, proudly proclaims herself as the “only MAGA candidate” in the primary, promising to keep the left-leaning state from continuing down a path toward “socialism.” The two GOP rivals also espoused similar conservative talking points about increasing government efficiency and accountability while reducing state spending and taxes.

For the quarter ending June 30, Aaron Guckian reported $9,088.49 in donations, $61,011.55 in spending and $30,190.38 in cash on hand. Elaine Pelino reported $2,124.99 in donations, $2,022.68 in spending and $3,142.95 in cash on hand. Second-quarter campaign finance reports were due to the Rhode Island Board of Elections by 11:59 p.m. on July 31.

The survey also took the pulse of 145 Republican primary voters in a three-way gubernatorial contest between Aaron Guckian, Elaine Pelino and Robert Raimondo, though Raimondo has since withdrawn. Pelino, a former comedian and first-time candidate, was backed by more than four in 10 primary voters, while Guckian, the state GOP’s endorsed candidate, received 17% support. Another four in 10 Republican primary voters were undecided, according to the survey. The margin of error for questions specific to Republican primary voters was 8.1%.

Guckian secured the Republican endorsement over primary rival Elaine Pelino by a 72-44 vote, with 10 participants opting not to endorse, according to information supplied by William Ricci Jr., secretary for the state party convention. Endorsements were made by secret ballot. Party-endorsed candidates get top placement on primary ballots.
